coupling.rationale: Modules meet through narrow interfaces: routes depend only on lib/data, lib/format, and components/partials; islands own their own DOM. Minor tangles: the build-render guard is smeared across every route, and document.client.ts is all-or-nothing.

app/src/components/partials.ts:77-79 — section/count/notFound partials make every resource page's skeleton reusable for a new Items section

abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions (Card, cardsForPokemon, partials, format helpers, fragment-refresh islands) stretch across five resource kinds with no boolean-flag creep; an Items section reuses most of it. Deductions: the route handler boilerplate would be copied a fifth time, and there's a little copy-paste (accessor trio, label lookup ×4).

findings.issue: spriteUrl reconstructs sprite paths from an ID pattern rather than using the API-provided sprites.front_default; if the sprite rule or data changes, Card must gain a sprite field, touching three producers (data.ts:174, :193, :261) plus partials.ts:24
findings.suggestion: Carry the sprite URL on Card (populate it once, e.g. in cardsForPokemon) so cardLink renders data rather than a pattern

findings.issue: The shared move-table renderer is exported from a route module while every other shared partial lives in components/partials.ts; anyone adding sortable tables elsewhere won't find it, and the export is used only inside the file
findings.suggestion: Move moveTables to components/partials.ts (or a components/move-tables.ts) and drop the export

findings.issue: The isBuildRender guard, 404-status assignment and document-title fallback are duplicated verbatim in all five routes, so changing the not-found or build-render convention is five synchronized edits
findings.suggestion: Extract a small withResource(loader) helper or a shared handler wrapper for the guard/status/title dance

findings.issue: Team-toggle button state (label, disabled, 'Team is full' note) is implemented twice: server template here and client #render in app/src/client/team-toggle.ts:36-47; a wording change needs both
findings.suggestion: Keep the server markup minimal and have the client element own the visible state, or derive the note text in one shared constant

findings.issue: The type-label lookup 'typeLabels.get(name) ?? humanize(name)' is repeated four times (data.ts:208, :384; pokemon/[name].ts:68; moves/[name].ts:32)
findings.suggestion: Add a labelFor(typeLabels, name) helper next to englishName in lib/format.ts

findings.issue: Filter-URL construction (omitting empty/default params) is implemented twice: server pagination links in routes/(home).ts:34-44 and the client history update here
findings.suggestion: Have the client submit the form and use the response URL, or share a small buildQuery helper between both sides

findings.issue: A single module-level AbortController is shared by every island; two fetching islands on one page would silently cancel each other's in-flight requests
findings.suggestion: Take the controller per call site (e.g. per island instance) instead of one module-global

findings.issue: All five island modules load on every page regardless of which islands are present
findings.suggestion: Give each route its own client entry or lazy-import islands, so adding a sixth island doesn't grow every page's bundle

summary: This is a well-factored Gracile app that's easy to own: data access, formatting, and card rendering each live in exactly one module, and client islands reuse server templates via fragment fetches instead of duplicating render logic. The costs are small and local: per-route handler boilerplate repeated five times, a shared helper stranded in a route file, and a handful of two-place duplications (team toggle state, filter URLs, type labels). Every scenario I traced landed in one to three predictable files with no dead-code traps beyond the ability accessor.
